clue.text: Is covered by a fairly customary benefit

parts.note: per means a, as in 'ten pounds a head' or 'per head'

indicators.note: being covered by something means sitting inside it, so the first piece goes within the following ones

parts.note: fairly means quite, as in 'quite good'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that something is protected by a reasonably standard perk.
explanation.walkthrough: IS goes inside PER QUITE, splitting QUITE after QU. PER for 'a' is the sense in 'once a week' = once per week.
explanation.definitionFit: A perk is an extra advantage that comes with a job by custom, which is what the longer word means.

clue.text: Invoice some academic or other

parts.note: a prof is a professor, an academic
taken as written
the other academic here is an MA, a Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A bill sent by some scholar or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some academic or other' reads as vague, but it is a list: a PROF, then OR, then another academic, an MA (Master of Arts).
explanation.definitionFit: A pro forma is a preliminary bill sent in advance of goods, so the phrase serves as a kind of invoice.

clue.text: Impossible to manage with empty negotiation

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Impossible to manage with empty negotiation (7)', is the tail of 3-down's clue repeated; no scan or reprint gives the real clue for RETREAT.
annotationWithheld.clue: Impossible to manage with empty negotiation

clue.text: Impossible to manage resolution of local trouble with empty negotiation

indicators.note: a resolution sorts things out anew, so the letters of the following words are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its outside letters, its contents removed

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood dispute that cannot be settled because talks have gone nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty negotiation' leaves NN, the first and last letters of 'negotiation'; 'resolution of' shuffles LOCAL, TROUBLE and NN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond control cannot be managed or restrained.

clue.text: Isn't she extremely silly mixing up combination?

indicators.note: extremely picks the extremes of the word, its first and last letters
mixing up the letters gives them a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe giving no letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a woman is being foolish in confusing things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely silly' gives SY, the first and last letters of 'silly'; 'mixing up' rearranges ISNTSHE with SY.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthesis is the joining of separate parts into one whole, a combination.

clue.text: Foreign street (in Turkey), comparatively straight

indicators.note: the street sits in Turkey, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey
rue is the French word for street

explanation.surface: A note on a road abroad, in Turkey, that is rather straighter than others.
explanation.walkthrough: RUE goes inside TR. TR is Turkey's code on cars and in internet addresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Truer can mean more exactly aligned or level, so more straight.

clue.text: Smoker initially satisfied about feature of pipe

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the word smoker
about here means turned round, so the word for satisfied runs backwards

parts.note: to meet a need is to satisfy it, so satisfied gives met

explanation.surface: A pipe smoker, content at first, considers a part of the pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: S from 'Smoker initially', then MET turned round by 'about' gives TEM.
explanation.definitionFit: The stem of a tobacco pipe is the tube between bowl and mouthpiece.

clue.text: Still time for consideration

parts.note: still and though both mean nevertheless

explanation.surface: A suggestion that there is more time left for reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb of time, but it means 'nevertheless', as does 'though'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought is careful reflection given to a matter, the act of considering it.

clue.text: Local bigwigs in Morayshire dropping rent, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly marks the remaining letters as turning up in an unexpected order
dropping means letting go of letters, which leave the county name

parts.note: to rent something is to hire it

explanation.surface: Town leaders in a Scottish county give up charging rent, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Morayshire is a former Scottish county. 'dropping' removes HIRE (rent) to leave MORAYS, and 'surprisingly' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayors are civic heads of towns, the leading figures in local government.

clue.text: Buildings occupied by force

parts.note: suggests property seized by violence, but the force is the police force, who work in these buildings

explanation.walkthrough: 'occupied by force' suggests a siege or squatters; the force is a police force, whose officers staff these buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: Police officers are based in these local offices, so the force occupies them every day.

clue.text: In which you could see Irish eye?

definitions.text: In which you could see Irish

explanation.surface: Someone wonders where an Irish eye might be glimpsed.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pubs an optic is the upturned bottle with a measuring valve behind the bar, so Irish whiskey is visible in it.
explanation.definitionFit: An optic is the bar device that dispenses spirits such as Irish whiskey through a clear measure; optic is also a humorous term for an eye.

clue.text: Take you longer to qualify for a medical specialism?

indicators.note: qualify can mean modify or change, so the letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a medical branch needs more years of training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to qualify' asks for YOU LONGER to be changed in form, so its letters are rearranged; 'Take' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Neurology is the branch of medicine dealing with the nervous system.

clue.text: Dismissed for being on strike

explanation.surface: Someone sacked for joining industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: A batter who is dismissed in cricket is out, and workers who have walked off the job are out too.

clue.text: Old church, Anglo-Norman in the main

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England
AN is the abbreviation for Anglo-Norman

explanation.surface: A historic church in a style of medieval architecture, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks like 'mostly', but 'the main' is an old poetic name for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic term for the high sea, the open water.

clue.text: Girl airline got rid of is not embarrassed

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
BA is British Airways
to shed something is to get rid of it

explanation.surface: A woman sacked by an airline shows no shame about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is only a link: the definition is 'not embarrassed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unabashed shows no shame or awkwardness at all.

clue.text: Needing doctor, getting pulse checked? It's not appropriate

parts.note: someone in need of a doctor is unwell
a pulse check means beats are counted against a clock

explanation.surface: A patient is unwell and having their pulse taken, which seems an awkward moment.
explanation.walkthrough: A doctor taking a pulse counts beats against a watch, so the pulse is TIMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at the wrong moment is unsuitable in its timing.

clue.text: On church and a castle icicles melted

indicators.note: melted things lose their shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ice hanging from a castle and a church thaws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'melted' rearranges A CASTLE ICICLES; 'On church' means 'concerning the church', an adjective as is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecclesiastical describes anything relating to the church or its clergy.

clue.text: Monk dumping federal agents in reservoir

indicators.note: dumping means discarding, so these letters are taken out of the monk

parts.note: a Cistercian is a monk of a strict Benedictine order
the CIA is the US federal intelligence agency

explanation.surface: A monk throws US spies into a reservoir.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove CIA from CISTERCIAN to leave CISTERN.
explanation.definitionFit: A cistern is a tank for storing water, a small reservoir.

clue.text: Irish playwright's work leading to complaint

explanation.surface: A dramatist's writing ends up causing illness.
explanation.walkthrough: The Irish playwright is Shaw; 'complaint' means a medical condition here, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Candida is a play by George Bernard Shaw, and candida is also the fungus behind thrush, a common ailment.

clue.text: New US pact is troublesome

indicators.note: a new version of the letters is a fresh arrangement of them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fresh American treaty causes problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges US PACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that acts up misbehaves or causes trouble, as a faulty machine does.

clue.text: Forecaster given no credit

parts.note: suggests a weather presenter left out of the credits, but means the Trojan prophetess whose true predictions nobody believed

explanation.walkthrough: 'credit' means belief here: the Greek myth's prophet of Troy was cursed never to be believed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the Trojan princess foretold disaster but was fated never to be believed.

clue.text: Appliance giving motorist less velocity

indicators.note: less means without, so the letter for velocity is removed

parts.note: a motorist is a driver
V is the symbol for velocity

explanation.surface: A gadget that makes a motorist slow down.
explanation.walkthrough: Take V from DRIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A drier is a household machine, such as a tumble drier, for removing moisture.

clue.text: Principle of which the corollary appears equally valid

indicators.text: of which the corollary appears equally valid
indicators.note: a word whose reverse reads just as well is the same backwards as forwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A rule whose consequences hold just as true.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is that the answer reads the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a belief or doctrine held as true.

clue.text: Runner appearing in abridged film

indicators.note: abridged means shortened, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: a skin is a thin film or layer

explanation.surface: An athlete features in a cut version of a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a movie, but it is a thin layer, SKIN, which loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is one of a pair of runners on which you glide over snow.

clue.text: Reportedly not caring for another pickled prawn?

indicators.note: reportedly signals that a word as said aloud gives the answer

parts.note: someone with no care for others is selfish

explanation.surface: Gossip about a crustacean in brine that shows no concern for others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' turns SELFISH into a word that sounds much like it. The question mark shows a pickled prawn is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A prawn is a crustacean, one of the creatures with hard outer cases eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Drug often misused originally (in that more scored)

indicators.note: the piece goes inside the letters just taken, which 'that' points back to
originally picks the opening letters of the two words

parts.note: piu is Italian for more, as written in musical scores

explanation.surface: A narcotic often abused from the start, with even more taken.
explanation.walkthrough: O and M from 'often misused originally' take PIU inside. 'scored' tells you 'more' is the musical marking, as in più forte.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium is a narcotic made from the poppy.

clue.text: Place bet in old money

explanation.surface: Gambling with outdated currency.
explanation.definitionFit: To punt is to make a wager, and the punt was the Irish pound before the euro.

clue.text: Lady holding up the train

parts.note: suggests a woman delaying a railway service, but means one carrying a wedding dress's trailing hem

explanation.walkthrough: The train is the long back of a wedding dress, carried by the bride's attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's attendant at a wedding often carries her long gown's trailing back.
